In the combined dataset that unifies the trees data with the income data by ZIP code, filling missing ZIP values where necessary, which three boroughs, restricted to records with median and mean income both greater than zero and a valid borough name, contain the highest number of trees, and what is the average mean income for each of these three boroughs?

SELECT 
    t.boroname,
    COUNT(*) as tree_count,
    AVG(it.Estimate_Mean_income) as avg_mean_income
FROM trees t
LEFT JOIN income_trees it ON t.zipcode = it.zipcode
WHERE it.Estimate_Median_income > 0

WITH borough_tree_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        t.boroname,
        COUNT(*) as total_trees
    FROM trees t
    LEFT JOIN income_trees i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
    WHERE t.boroname IS NOT NULL
        AND i.Estimate_Median_income IS NOT NULL
        AND i.Estimate_Mean_income IS NOT NULL
        AND i.Estimate_Median_income > 0
        AND i.Estimate_Mean_income > 0
    GROUP BY t.boroname
),
top_three_boroughs AS (
    SELECT boroname
    FROM borough_tree_counts
    ORDER BY total_trees DESC
    LIMIT 3
),
borough_avg_income AS (
    SELECT 
        t.boroname,
        AVG(CAST(i.Estimate_Mean_income AS REAL)) as avg_mean_income
    FROM trees t
    LEFT JOIN income_trees i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
    WHERE t.boroname IS NOT NULL
        AND i.Estimate_Median_income IS NOT NULL
        AND i.Estimate_Mean_income IS NOT NULL
        AND i.Estimate_Median_income > 0
        AND i.Estimate_Mean_income > 0
        AND t.boroname IN (SELECT boroname FROM top_three_boroughs)
    GROUP BY t.boroname
)
SELECT b.boroname, a.avg_mean_income
FROM borough_avg_income a
JOIN borough_tree_counts b ON a.boroname = b.boroname
ORDER BY b.total_trees DESC
